groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–2 题
groups.material: A poisonous fish which has a sting strong enough to kill a human is invading the Mediterranean, warn scientists. The International Union for Conservation of Nature has raised concerns after the poisonous fish was spotted in the waters around Turkey, Cyprus, and the eastern Mediterranean. Native to the South Pacific and Indian Ocean, the potentially deadly fish has poisonous hooks and a painful sting capable of killing people. Although fatalities are rare, the stings can cause extreme pain and stop people breathing. The fish, often known as Devil Firefish, is a highly invasive species, and environmentalists fear its arrival could endanger other types of marine life. After being spotted in the Mediterranean, a marine scientist says, "The fish is spreading, and that's a cause for concern."

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 3–4 题
groups.material: Almost half the center of Paris will be accessible only by foot or bicycle this Sunday to mark World Car-Free Day. This is in response to rising air pollution that made Paris the most polluted city in the world for a brief time. Mayor Anne Hidalgo promoted the first World Car-Free Day last year. Hidalgo also has supported a "Paris Breathes" day. On the first Sunday of every month, Paris clears traffic from eight lanes of the main road. About 400 miles of streets will be closed to cars. It is expected to bring significant reduction in pollution levels. Last year's car-free day showed a 40 percent drop in pollution levels in some parts of the city, according to an independent air pollution monitor, reports The Guardian—and sound levels dropped by 50 percent in the city's center.

groups.title: Section A · 第 3 篇 · 5–7 题
groups.material: A Philippine fisherman was feeling down on his luck when a house fire forced him to clear out his possessions and change locations. Then a good luck charm that he had kept under his bed changed his life. The unidentified man had fished out a giant pearl from the ocean when his anchor got stuck on the rock while sailing off the coastal island in the Philippines ten years ago. When he was forced to sell it, the shocked tourist agent at Puerto Princesa told him that the 77-pound giant pearl that he'd kept hidden in his run-down wooden house was the biggest pearl in the world, which was valued at 76 million pounds. The pearl of Allah, which is currently on display in a New York museum only weighs 14 pounds. That is 5 times smaller than the pearl that the fisherman just handed in. The monstrous pearl measured at one foot wide and 2.2 feet long is going to be verified by local experts and international authorities before hopefully going on display to attract more tourists in the little town.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 8–11 题
groups.material:
W: Mr. Smith, it's a pleasure meeting you.
M: Nice to meet you, too. What can I do for you?
W: Well, I'm here to show you what our firm can do for you. Astra Consultants has branches in over 50 countries, offering different business services. We are a global company with 75 years of history, and our clients include some of the world's largest companies.
M: Thank you, Mrs. Houston. I know Astra Consultants is a famous company. But you said you would show me what you could do for me. Well, what exactly can your firm do for my company?
W: We advise businesses on all matters, from market analysis to legal issues, anything a business like yours could need. Our firm offers expert advice. Could I ask you, Mr. Smith, to tell me a little about your company and the challenges you face? That way I could better respond as to how we can help you.
M: Okay, sure. This is a family business started by my grandfather in 1950. We employ just over 100 people. We manufacture and export stone for buildings and other constructions. Our clients usually want a special kind of stone cut in a special design. And that's what we do in our factory. Our main challenge is that our national currency is rising, and we're losing competitive advantage to stone producers in India.
W: I see. That's very interesting. I would suggest that you let us first conduct a financial analysis of your company, together with an analysis of your competitors in India. That way we could offer the best advice on different ways forward for you.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
W: Wow, congratulations, Simon! The place looks absolutely amazing!
M: Really? You think so?
W: Of course. I love it. It looks like you had a professional interior designer. But you didn't, did you?
M: No. I did it all by myself with a little help from my brother Greg. He's actually in the construction business, which was really helpful.
W: I honestly am impressed. I know I could probably repaint the walls in my house over a weekend or something, but not a full renovation. Where did you get your ideas? I wouldn't know where to start.
M: Well, for a while now, I've been regularly buying home design magazines. Every now and then, I'd save a picture I liked. Believe it or not, I had a full notebook of magazine pages. Since my overall style was quite minimal, I thought and hoped a whole renovation wouldn't be too difficult. And sure enough, with Greg's help, it was very achievable.
W: Was it very expensive? I've imagined a project like this could be.
M: Actually it was surprisingly affordable. I managed to sell a lot of my old furniture and put that extra money towards the new material. Greg was also able to get some discount materials from a recent project he was working on as well.
W: Great. If you don't mind, I'd like to pick your brains a bit more. Jonathan and I are thinking of renovating our sitting room, not the whole house, not yet anyway. And we'd love to get some inspiration from your experience. Are you free to come over for a coffee early next week?

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material: Removing foreign objects from ears and noses costs England almost three million pounds a year, a study suggests. Children were responsible for the vast majority of cases—95% of objects removed from noses and 85% from ears. Every year an average of 1,218 nose and 2,479 ear removals took place between 2010 and 2016. According to England's Hospital Episode Statistics, children aged one to four were the most likely to need help from doctors for a foreign object in their nose. Five- to nine-year-olds come to the hospital with something in their ears the most. Jewellery items accounted for up to 40% of cases in both the ears and noses of children. Paper and plastic toys were the items removed next most from noses. Cotton buds and pencils were also found in ears. According to the study, the occurrence of foreign objects in children is generally attributed to curiosity. Children have an impulse to explore their noses and ears. This resulted in the accidental entry of foreign objects. Any ear, nose and throat surgeon has many weird stories about wonderful objects found in the noses and ears of children and adults. Batteries can pose a particular danger. In all cases prevention is better than cure. This is why many toys contain warnings about small parts. Recognizing problems early and seeking medical attention is important.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material: Good morning. Today, I would like to talk to you about my charity ReBicycle. But before that, let me introduce someone. This is Leila Rahimi. She was so scared when she first moved to New Zealand that she struggled to leave the house and would spend days working up the courage to walk to the supermarket for basic supplies. After a few months of being quite down and unhappy, she was invited to join a local bike club. At this time, ReBicycle got involved and gave Leila a second-hand bicycle. Within weeks, her depression had begun to ease as she cycled. The bicycle totally changed her life, giving her hope and a true feeling of freedom. To date, ReBicycle has donated more than 200 bikes to those in need, and is now expanding bike-riding lessons as demand soars. With a bike, newcomers here can travel farther but for almost no cost. The three hours a day, they used to spend walking to and from English language lessons, have been reduced to just one hour. Our bike-riding lessons are so successful that we are urgently looking for more volunteers. Learning to ride a bike is almost always more difficult for an adult, and this can take days and weeks, rather than hours. So if any of you have some free time during the weekend, please come join us at ReBicycle and make a difference in someone's life.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material: Thanks to the International Space Station, we know quite a bit about the effects of low gravity on the human body, but NASA scientists want to learn more. To that end, they have been studying how other species deal with low gravity, specifically focusing on mice. The results are both interesting and humorous. The scientists first sent some mice in a specially designed cage to the International Space Station. The cage allowed them to study the behavior of the mice remotely from Earth via video. As you'll notice in the video, the mice definitely seem uncomfortable at the beginning of the experiment. They move around clumsily, drifting within the small confines of the cage, and do their best to figure out which way is up, but without success. However, it's not long before the mice begin to catch on. They adapt remarkably well to their new environment and even use the lack of gravity to their advantage as they push themselves around the cage. That's when things really get wild. The eleventh day of the experiment shows the mice are not just dealing with the gravity change but actually seem to be enjoying it. Several of the mice are observed running around the cage walls. The scientists wanted to see whether the mice would continue doing the same kinds of activities they were observed doing on Earth. The study showed that the mice kept much of their routines intact, including cleaning themselves and eating when hungry.

questions.prompt: What is reported in the news?
options: Many people have been attacked by Devil Firefish.
The Mediterranean is a natural habitat of Devil Firefish.
Invasive species are driving away certain native species.
A deadly fish has been spotted in the Mediterranean waters.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is reported in the news? 

 【翻译】 新闻报道了什么? 
 A)  许多人遭到魔鬼火鱼的攻击。 
 B)  地中海是魔鬼火鱼的天然栖息地。 
 C)  入侵物种正在驱逐某些本地物种。 
 D)  地中海水域发现了一种致命鱼类。 

 【答案】 D （主旨题） A deadly fish has been spotted in the Mediterranean waters. 
 【定位】 P1 A poisonous fish which has a sting strong enough to kill a human is invading the Mediterranean, warn scientists. 
 科学家警告说，一种毒刺强到足以杀死人类的毒鱼正在入侵地中海。 

 【信号】 新闻首句即导语 。答案就在录音第一句 A poisonous fish which has a sting strong enough to kill a human is invading the Mediterranean。新闻的开头第一句是"导语"，按惯例把"什么东西、在哪、发生了什么"一次性压缩说完，主旨题的答案几乎必在这里，不必等后文。 

 【替换】 A poisonous fish which has a sting strong enough to kill a human ↔ A deadly fish 毒到能致命＝deadly 
 is invading the Mediterranean ↔ has been spotted in the Mediterranean waters 正在入侵＝已被发现于该海域 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 录音只说毒刺"强到足以杀人"、且明说 fatalities are rare（致死案例罕见），并没说"很多人已被攻击"。选项 Many people have been attacked 盗用了录音里 kill a human、sting 的危险氛围，把"有杀人的潜力"偷换成"很多人已遭攻击"，是无中生有的夸大。  借用原文：Although fatalities are rare, the stings can cause extreme pain and stop people breathing 

 B) 与原文相反 录音明说这鱼 Native to the South Pacific and Indian Ocean（原产南太平洋和印度洋），是"入侵"地中海，恰恰说明地中海不是它的天然栖息地。选项 The Mediterranean is a natural habitat 盗用了 the Mediterranean 这个高频地名，却把"入侵地"歪曲成"原产地"，与原文相反。  借用原文：Native to the South Pacific and Indian Ocean, the potentially deadly fish has poisonous hooks 

 C) 过度推断 录音只说环保人士"担心"这鱼"could endanger"其他海洋生物（还没发生），选项 Invasive species are driving away certain native species 用现在时把"可能危及"说成"正在赶走本地物种"这一既成事实，且 Invasive species 用复数泛指多种入侵物种，与本则只报道一种鱼的范围不符。它盗用了 invasive 这个原词。  借用原文：environmentalists fear its arrival could endanger other types of marine life
questions.spoken_text: What is reported in the news?

questions.prompt: What is the environmentalist concerned about the spread of Devil Firefish in the Mediterranean?
options: It could badly pollute the surrounding waters.
It could pose a threat to other marine species.
It could disrupt the food chains there.
It could add to greenhouse emissions.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the environmentalist concerned about the spread of Devil Firefish in the Mediterranean? 

 【翻译】 环保主义者对魔鬼火鱼在地中海扩散有何担忧? 
 A)  它可能严重污染周围水域。 
 B)  它可能对其他海洋物种构成威胁。 
 C)  它可能破坏那里的食物链。 
 D)  它可能增加温室气体排放。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It could pose a threat to other marine species. 
 【定位】 P1 The fish, often known as Devil Firefish, is a highly invasive species, and environmentalists fear its arrival could endanger other types of marine life. 
 这种鱼通常被称为"魔鬼蓑鲉"，是一种高度入侵性的物种，环保人士担心它的到来可能危及其他类型的海洋生物。 

 【信号】 fear＋题干同源词触发定位 。答案句里 environmentalists fear 的 fear（担心）与题干的 concerned（担心）是同一意思，这个"担忧"信号词一响，紧跟其后的 could endanger other types of marine life 就是担忧的具体内容——担忧类细节题，答案永远在"担心"这个词后面那个对象上。 

 【替换】 could endanger other types of marine life ↔ pose a threat to other marine species 危及＝构成威胁 
 other types of marine life ↔ other marine species 海洋生物＝海洋物种 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 录音通篇只说这鱼"有毒、毒刺能伤人、会危及其他海洋生物"，从没提它会"污染水体"。选项 badly pollute the surrounding waters 是考生听到"poisonous（有毒）"后顺着常识联想出的"有毒→污染水"，但原文根本没这句话。 
 C) 过度推断 disrupt the food chains（扰乱食物链）听上去比"威胁生物"更像专业的环保表述，很能唬人；但录音对担忧的描述只到 endanger other types of marine life 为止，没有展开到"食物链"这一层。它是"听起来更高级、更该说"造成的诱惑，并非原文内容。 
 D) 未提及 add to greenhouse emissions（增加温室气体排放）和"毒鱼威胁海洋生物"这个话题毫不相干，录音从头到尾没提温室气体或气候，是明显的凑数干扰项。
questions.spoken_text: What is the environmentalist's concern about the spread of devil firefish in the Mediterranean?

questions.prompt: What will happen on World Car-Free Day in Paris?
options: Cars will not be allowed to enter the city.
Pedestrians will have free access to the city.
About half of its city center will be closed to cars.
Buses will be the only vehicles allowed on its streets.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What will happen on World Car-Free Day in Paris? 

 【翻译】 巴黎的世界无车日将会发生什么? 
 A)  汽车将不被允许进入该城市。 
 B)  行人将可以免费进入该城市。 
 C)  该城市约一半的市中心将对汽车关闭。 
 D)  公共汽车将是其街道上唯一允许通行的车辆。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） About half of its city center will be closed to cars. 
 【定位】 P1 Almost half the center of Paris will be accessible only by foot or bicycle this Sunday to mark World Car-Free Day. 
 本周日，巴黎市中心将近一半的区域只能靠步行或骑自行车进入，以此纪念"世界无车日"。 

 【信号】 新闻首句直接点出当天安排 。新闻往往开门见山，第一句 Almost half the center of Paris will be accessible only by foot or bicycle this Sunday 就交代了无车日当天的核心安排——"市中心近一半只能步行或骑车进入"。这正是"那天会怎样"的答案句，信号就是它处在新闻开头、与题干"What will happen"直接对应。 

 【替换】 Almost half the center of Paris will be accessible only by foot or bicycle ↔ About half of its city center will be closed to cars. 正面"只能步行骑车"＝反面"对汽车关闭" 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 说 Cars will not be allowed to enter the city.，盗用了录音里的 "Paris" 和"汽车不能进"的意思，但把范围从"近一半市中心"（Almost half the center of Paris）偷偷放大到"整座城市（the city）"。录音明明说的是"half the center"，A 漏掉了"half"和"center"这两个范围限定，范围被夸大，故错。  借用原文：Almost half the center of Paris 

 B) 未提及 B 说 Pedestrians will have free access to the city.。录音只说"只能靠步行或自行车进入"（accessible only by foot or bicycle），意思是"限定方式"，根本没提行人"free（免费/免许可）"。"free"是录音里没有的信息，属于无中生有。 
 D) 偷换概念 D 说 Buses will be the only vehicles allowed on its streets.。录音说当天"只能靠步行或自行车"进入（only by foot or bicycle），allowed 的是 foot/bicycle，根本没提 buses。D 借用了"only…allowed"的句式结构来唬人，却把允许的对象从"步行、自行车"偷换成了"公交车"，张冠李戴。  借用原文：accessible only by foot or bicycle
questions.spoken_text: What will happen on World Car Free Day in Paris?

questions.prompt: What motivated the mayor of Paris to promote the first World Car-Free Day in her city?
options: The unbearable traffic noise.
The worsening global warming.
The ever-growing cost of petrol.
The rising air pollution in Paris.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What motivated the mayor of Paris to promote the first World Car-Free Day in her city? 

 【翻译】 是什么促使巴黎市长在她的城市推动首个世界无车日? 
 A)  难以忍受的交通噪音。 
 B)  日益恶化的全球变暖。 
 C)  不断增长的汽油成本。 
 D)  巴黎不断上升的空气污染。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） The rising air pollution in Paris. 
 【定位】 P1 This is in response to rising air pollution that made Paris the most polluted city in the world for a brief time. 
 这是为了应对不断加剧的空气污染——这种污染曾一度让巴黎成为世界上污染最严重的城市。 

 【信号】 因果信号 in response to 引出动机 。答案句靠 in response to（为了应对……）这个明确的因果信号锁定。"This is in response to rising air pollution"——"应对不断加剧的空气污染"正是搞无车日的动机。听到 "in response to" 就知道后面紧跟的就是原因，无需犹豫。 

 【替换】 in response to rising air pollution ↔ The rising air pollution in Paris. 几乎原句搬选项，仅补回地点 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 说 The unbearable traffic noise.。录音确实在结尾提到了声音——"sound levels dropped by 50 percent"，但那是无车日带来的"效果"，而且是"声音降了"，不是"难以忍受的噪音"促使办无车日。A 盗用了录音里关于 sound 的内容，却把"结果"错当成"动机"，答非所问。  借用原文：sound levels dropped by 50 percent in the city's center 

 B) 未提及 B 说 The worsening global warming.。"global warming（全球变暖）"在整段录音里从未出现，是凭"环保话题就该和变暖有关"的常识硬塞进来的。录音给的动机明确是 air pollution，不是 global warming。 
 C) 未提及 C 说 The ever-growing cost of petrol.。"cost of petrol（油价）"录音里完全没提，同样是"汽车／环保话题常和油价挂钩"的想当然。录音说的动机是空气污染，与油价无关。
questions.spoken_text: What motivates the mayor of Paris to promote the first World Car Free Day in her city?

questions.prompt: What happened to the Philippine fisherman one day?
options: His house was burnt down in a fire.
Many of his possessions were stolen.
His good luck charm sank into the sea.
His fishing boat got wrecked on a rock.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What happened to the Philippine fisherman one day? 

 【翻译】 菲律宾渔民有一天发生了什么事？ 
 A)  他的房子在一场火灾中被烧毁了。 
 B)  他的许多财物被盗了。 
 C)  他的幸运符沉入了海里。 
 D)  他的渔船在一块岩石上失事了。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） His house was burnt down in a fire. 
 【定位】 P1 A Philippine fisherman was feeling down on his luck when a house fire forced him to clear out his possessions and change locations. 
 一名菲律宾渔夫正觉得自己运气背，这时一场房屋火灾迫使他清空家当、搬离原地。 

 【信号】 录音开篇第一句即点事件 。新闻往往把核心事件放在开篇，这里第一句 a house fire forced him to clear out his possessions 就直接交代了发生的事——一场房屋火灾。新闻题与播报同序，第 5 题问“发生了什么”，答案就落在最先念出的这句。 

 【替换】 a house fire forced him to clear out his possessions ↔ His house was burnt down in a fire house fire 与 burnt down in a fire 同义 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 录音里确有 possessions 一词，forced him to clear out his possessions 说的是火灾逼他“清理/搬走”家当，不是被偷。选项 Many of his possessions were stolen. 盗用了 possessions 这个原词，却把“清空”偷换成 stolen（被偷），听到 possessions 就选会中招。  借用原文：clear out his possessions 

 C) 原词陷阱 录音确实提到 good luck charm（护身符）和 ocean/sea，a good luck charm that he had kept under his bed，但护身符是放在床下、并由海里捞出，从未沉入海中。选项 His good luck charm sank into the sea. 拼接了 charm 和 sea 两个原词，编出一个录音没说的事件。  借用原文：a good luck charm that he had kept under his bed 

 D) 原词陷阱 录音里 rock 确实出现，his anchor got stuck on the rock 说的是“船锚卡在岩石上”，因此捞起了珍珠，渔船并没有触礁损毁。选项 His fishing boat got wrecked on a rock. 盗用了 rock 这个原词，把“锚卡石头”夸大成“船触礁失事”，与录音不符。  借用原文：his anchor got stuck on the rock
questions.spoken_text: What happened to the Philippine fisherman one day?

questions.prompt: What was the fisherman forced to do?
options: Change his fishing locations.
Find a job in a travel agency.
Sell the pearl he had kept for years.
Spend a few nights on a small island.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What was the fisherman forced to do? 

 【翻译】 这位渔民被迫做什么？ 
 A)  改变他的捕鱼地点。 
 B)  在一家旅行社找一份工作。 
 C)  出售他保存多年的珍珠。 
 D)  在一个小岛上度过几个晚上。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Sell the pearl he had kept for years. 
 【定位】 P1 When he was forced to sell it, the shocked tourist agent at Puerto Princesa told him that the 77-pound giant pearl ... was the biggest pearl in the world. 
 当他被迫卖掉这颗珍珠时，普林塞萨港那位震惊的旅游代理告诉他，这颗 77 磅的巨型珍珠是世界上最大的珍珠。 

 【信号】 题干强制语 forced 在原文原样出现 。题干问 forced to do，录音里出现 When he was forced to sell it——forced 这个强制语在原文照样念出，它后面紧跟的动词 sell 就是答案动作。强制语原词重现是最直接的定位信号。 

 【替换】 When he was forced to sell it ↔ Sell the pearl he had kept for years sell it 与 Sell the pearl 同指 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音里 change locations 确实念到，forced him to clear out his possessions and change locations 指火灾后“搬家/换住处”，不是换打鱼的地方。选项 Change his fishing locations. 盗用 change locations 并擅自加上 fishing，把“搬家”偷换成“换渔场”。  借用原文：change locations

 pick your brains a bit more ↔ share his renovation experience with her 习语pick your brains=取经 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 talk with Jonathan about a new project 偷用原文人名 Jonathan（Jonathan and I are thinking of renovating）——但 Jonathan 是和她一起想翻新客厅的人，她从没说请男士去「和 Jonathan 谈一个新项目」。听到 Jonathan 就选是陷阱。  借用原文：Jonathan and I are thinking of renovating 

 B) 与原文相反 show him around her newly-renovated house 说带他参观她「已翻新」的家——但她明说 thinking of renovating our sitting room, not the whole house, not yet anyway，是「正打算翻、还没翻」。把她还没做的事说成已完成，是时态 / 事实陷阱。  借用原文：not the whole house, not yet anyway 

 C) 未提及 discuss the house decoration budget 里 budget 是钱的话题，蹭了前文谈花费（affordable）的印象——但她请他来是为取经，全程没提要和他谈「预算」。这是把别处的话题硬搬过来。

questions.prompt: What does England spend an annual three million pounds on?
options: Paying hospital bills for emergency cases.
Doing research on ear, nose and throat diseases.
Removing objects from patients' noses and ears.
Providing routine care for small children.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does England spend an annual three million pounds on? 

 【翻译】 英格兰每年在什么方面花费三百万英镑？ 
 A)  支付急诊病例的住院费用。 
 B)  研究耳鼻喉疾病。 
 C)  从患者的鼻子和耳朵中取出异物。 
 D)  为幼儿提供常规护理。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Removing objects from patients' noses and ears. 
 【定位】 P1 Removing foreign objects from ears and noses costs England almost three million pounds a year, a study suggests. 
 一项研究显示，从耳朵和鼻子里取出异物每年要花费英国近三百万英镑。 

 【信号】 花费数字句——costs…three million pounds 。答案句的信号是"动作 + 花费 + 三百万"这一结构：Removing foreign objects from ears and noses costs England almost three million pounds a year 直接把题干里的 three million pounds 和它的用途（取异物）绑在一句，听到 costs…three million pounds 就锁定这是答案句。 

 【替换】 Removing foreign objects from ears and noses ↔ Removing objects from patients' noses and ears. foreign objects=objects、词序调换的同义改写 

 【排除】 A) 答非所问 录音通篇在讲医院取异物，孩子会联想到"付医院账单"，但原文从未说这三百万是用来 Paying hospital bills for emergency cases.，只说花在"取异物"这个动作上，付账单是凭"医院"二字脑补出来的。 
 B) 原词陷阱 录音后文确实出现 Any ear, nose and throat surgeon，选项 Doing research on ear, nose and throat diseases. 原样搬来 ear, nose and throat 这串词，但那是在讲外科医生的奇闻，不是说三百万花在"做研究"上，听到熟词就选会中招。  借用原文：Any ear, nose and throat surgeon has many weird stories 

 D) 原词陷阱 录音反复提到 children，选项 Providing routine care for small children. 借这个高频词编出"日常护理"，但原文说钱花在"取异物"这个具体动作上，从没说花在"日常护理"，属拿熟词编新用途。  借用原文：Children were responsible for the vast majority of cases

questions.prompt: What do we learn from England's Hospital Episode Statistics?
options: Children aged one to four are often more curious than older children.
Five- to nine-year-olds are the most likely to put things in their ears.
Many children like to put foreign objects in their mouths.
Many children like to smell things they find or play with.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn from England's Hospital Episode Statistics? 

 【翻译】 我们从英格兰医院事件统计中了解到什么？ 
 A)  一到四岁的儿童往往比年龄较大的儿童更有好奇心。 
 B)  五到九岁的儿童最有可能把东西塞进耳朵里。 
 C)  许多儿童喜欢把异物放进嘴里。 
 D)  许多儿童喜欢闻他们找到或玩耍的东西。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Five- to nine-year-olds are the most likely to put things in their ears. 
 【定位】 P1 According to England's Hospital Episode Statistics, children aged one to four were the most likely to need help from doctors for a foreign object in their nose. Five- to nine-year-olds come to the hospital with something in their ears the most. 
 根据英国医院病例统计，1 到 4 岁的儿童最有可能因为鼻子里有异物而需要医生帮助。5 到 9 岁的儿童最常因为耳朵里有东西而到医院就诊。 

 【信号】 专有名词 + 两个年龄段并列 。信号是题干专有名词的原样复现 According to England's Hospital Episode Statistics，紧接其后是两句年龄段并列陈述，把"1-4 岁→鼻""5-9 岁→耳"分别说清，正是要核对的答案句。 

 【替换】 Five- to nine-year-olds come to the hospital with something in their ears the most ↔ Five- to nine-year-olds are the most likely to put things in their ears. come to hospital with…the most=most likely to put…，结果换说成行为 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音确有 children aged one to four were the most likely to need help…for a foreign object in their nose，但说的是"1-4 岁→鼻子"，选项 Children aged one to four are often more curious than older children. 盗用了 one to four 这个年龄段，却把后半改成原文没说的"比大孩子更好奇"，年龄对、结论错。  借用原文：children aged one to four were the most likely to need help from doctors for a foreign object in their nose 

 C) 偷换概念 录音只讲鼻（nose）和耳（ears），选项 Many children like to put foreign objects in their mouths. 借 foreign objects 这个原词，却把部位换成了"嘴 mouths"，原文从未说孩子往嘴里塞东西。  借用原文：Removing foreign objects from ears and noses 

 D) 未提及 选项 Many children like to smell things they find or play with. 说孩子"喜欢闻东西"，但这份统计句里只讲塞鼻塞耳、就医取物，全篇都没提"smell（闻）"这个行为，属凭"鼻子"联想脑补。

questions.prompt: What is generally believed to account for children putting things in their ears or noses?
options: They want to attract attention.
They tend to act out of impulse.
They are unaware of the potential risks.
They are curious about these body parts.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is generally believed to account for children putting things in their ears or noses? 

 【翻译】 人们普遍认为儿童把东西塞进耳朵或鼻子的原因是什么？ 
 A)  他们想吸引注意力。 
 B)  他们往往出于冲动行事。 
 C)  他们没有意识到潜在的风险。 
 D)  他们对这些身体部位感到好奇。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） They are curious about these body parts. 
 【定位】 P1 According to the study, the occurrence of foreign objects in children is generally attributed to curiosity. Children have an impulse to explore their noses and ears. 
 根据这项研究，儿童体内出现异物的情况通常被归因于好奇心。孩子有一种探索自己鼻子和耳朵的冲动。 

 【信号】 因果信号 attributed to 后面的 curiosity 。答案信号是因果短语 is generally attributed to curiosity——attributed to（归因于）正是"导致原因"的信号，它后面紧跟的 curiosity 就是公认原因，听到 attributed to 立刻锁定其后那个词。 

 【替换】 is generally attributed to curiosity ↔ They are curious about these body parts. 名词 curiosity ↔ 形容词 curious，名词转形容词 
 Children have an impulse to explore their noses and ears ↔ curious about these body parts "想探索鼻耳"="对这些身体部位好奇"，详述换概括 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 选项 They want to attract attention. 把原因说成"想引起注意"，但录音归因句明说原因是 curiosity，全篇没提 attract attention，属另起一个原文没有的原因。 
 B) 原词陷阱 录音确有 Children have an impulse to explore their noses and ears，选项 They tend to act out of impulse. 原样搬来 impulse 这个词，但原文的"冲动"是"探索鼻耳的冲动"、用来佐证好奇，并非把"一时冲动"本身当作公认原因，题目问的公认原因是 curiosity。  借用原文：Children have an impulse to explore their noses and ears 

 C) 原词陷阱 录音后文提到 Batteries can pose a particular danger，让"没意识到风险"显得合理，但选项 They are unaware of the potential risks. 说的"没意识到危险"原文从未当作孩子塞东西的原因，公认原因是好奇，这是把后文的"危险"错接成原因。  借用原文：Batteries can pose a particular danger

questions.prompt: What did ReBicycle do to help Leila Rahimi?
options: It gave her a used bicycle.
It paid for her English lessons.
It delivered her daily necessities.
It provided her with physical therapy.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did ReBicycle do to help Leila Rahimi? 

 【翻译】 ReBicycle 做了什么来帮助 Leila Rahimi? 
 A)  它给了她一辆二手自行车。 
 B)  它支付了她的英语课程费用。 
 C)  它配送了她的日常生活必需品。 
 D)  它为她提供了物理治疗。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） It gave her a used bicycle. 
 【定位】 P1 At this time, ReBicycle got involved and gave Leila a second-hand bicycle. 
 就在这时，ReBicycle 介入进来，给了 Leila 一辆二手自行车。 

 【信号】 人名出场后紧跟的动作句 。题干点的人名 Leila 在原文反复出现，而真正承载「为她做了什么」的，是 ReBicycle got involved and gave Leila a second-hand bicycle 这句——机构名 ReBicycle 与人名 Leila 同时出现、又带了 gave 这个给予动作，正是答案句的信号。 

 【替换】 a second-hand bicycle ↔ a used bicycle second-hand = used 同义替换 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 原文确实提到 English language lessons，但那是说有了车之后通勤去上英语课的时间从三小时减到一小时，机构并没有为 Leila 付英语课学费。B 项 It paid for her English lessons. 把听到的 English lessons 原词搬过来，却安了个原文没有的 paid for，是典型「听到原词就想选」的陷阱。  借用原文：they used to spend walking to and from English language lessons 

 C) 原词陷阱 原文里 Leila 起初是自己 walk to the supermarket for basic supplies（走去超市买生活必需品），这是说她从前的困境，并非机构帮她送货。C 项 It delivered her daily necessities. 借用了 supplies/necessities 这层「生活必需品」的原词印象，编出一个机构「配送」的动作，实际机构给的是车不是货。  借用原文：walk to the supermarket for basic supplies 

 D) 过度推断 原文说 Leila 骑车后 her depression had begun to ease（抑郁开始缓解），这是骑车带来的心理变化，并不等于机构提供了 physical therapy（理疗）。D 项 It provided her with physical therapy. 抓住「身体/康复」的联想做了过度推断，原文从没说过理疗。
questions.spoken_text: What did Re-Bicycle do to help Leila Rahimi?

questions.prompt: What is ReBicycle doing to help those in need?
options: Expanding bike-riding lessons.
Providing free public transport.
Offering walking tours to visitors.
Asking local people for donations.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is ReBicycle doing to help those in need? 

 【翻译】 ReBicycle 正在做什么来帮助那些有需要的人? 
 A)  扩大自行车骑行课程。 
 B)  提供免费公共交通。 
 C)  为游客提供步行游览。 
 D)  向当地居民募捐。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Expanding bike-riding lessons. 
 【定位】 P1 To date, ReBicycle has donated more than 200 bikes to those in need, and is now expanding bike-riding lessons as demand soars. 
 迄今为止，ReBicycle 已向有需要的人捐赠了 200 多辆自行车，如今正随着需求激增而扩大自行车骑行课程。 

 【信号】 now + 进行时标出当下举措 。句中 is now expanding bike-riding lessons 同时含 now 和进行时 is expanding，正是「当下正在做的举措」的信号；题干 those in need 也原样出现在这句，双重提示这就是答案句。 

 【替换】 is now expanding bike-riding lessons ↔ Expanding bike-riding lessons. 几乎原句压缩，去掉时态助词 

 【排除】 B) 偷换概念 原文讲的是给人自行车、让人能 travel farther but for almost no cost（几乎零成本走得更远），核心是「自行车」。B 项 Providing free public transport. 借「免费、出行」的听感，把自行车偷换成 public transport（公共交通），概念被掉包，原文从未说提供公共交通。  借用原文：travel farther but for almost no cost 

 C) 原词陷阱 原文提到人们从前 they used to spend walking（过去常常靠走路）通勤，是要被自行车取代的旧状态。C 项 Offering walking tours to visitors. 抓住 walking 这个原词，编出「为游客提供步行游」，既反了原文（机构是要减少走路、不是组织走路），也无中生有了 visitors。  借用原文：The three hours a day, they used to spend walking to and from English language lessons 

 D) 偷换概念 原文说机构 urgently looking for more volunteers（急招志愿者），求的是人手不是钱。D 项 Asking local people for donations. 把「求助于本地人」这层意思保留，却把要的东西换成 donations（捐款），张冠李戴成募捐，原文没有向人要钱。  借用原文：we are urgently looking for more volunteers

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the passage about ReBicycle?
options: It is a sports club.
It is a language school.
It is a counseling center.
It is a charity organization.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn from the passage about ReBicycle? 

 【翻译】 我们从文章中了解到关于 ReBicycle 的什么信息? 
 A)  它是一个体育俱乐部。 
 B)  它是一所语言学校。 
 C)  它是一个咨询中心。 
 D)  它是一个慈善组织。 

 【答案】 D （主旨题） It is a charity organization. 
 【定位】 P1 Today, I would like to talk to you about my charity ReBicycle. ... To date, ReBicycle has donated more than 200 bikes to those in need ... we are urgently looking for more volunteers. 
 今天我想跟大家谈谈我的慈善机构 ReBicycle。……迄今为止，ReBicycle 已向有需要的人捐赠了 200 多辆自行车……我们正急切地寻找更多志愿者。 

 【信号】 开头自报性质 + 全篇行为印证 。开篇 my charity ReBicycle 直接点明它是 charity（慈善机构），再由 has donated more than 200 bikes to those in need 免费捐车、looking for more volunteers 招募志愿者等行为印证——开头点题加全篇行为合起来锁定性质，是主旨题的定位信号。 

 【替换】 my charity ReBicycle ↔ a charity organization charity → charity organization 概括化 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 原文提到 Leila 曾被邀请加入 a local bike club（当地一个自行车俱乐部），那是另一个组织，不是 ReBicycle 本身。A 项 It is a sports club. 借 bike club 的「俱乐部/运动」印象，把 ReBicycle 错认成体育俱乐部，张冠李戴到了别的组织头上。  借用原文：she was invited to join a local bike club 

 B) 原词陷阱 原文里 English language lessons 只是用来说明有了车之后通勤时间缩短，机构本身不教英语。B 项 It is a language school. 抓 English lessons 的原词，把机构错定成语言学校，原文从未说它是教语言的学校。  借用原文：walking to and from English language lessons 

 C) 过度推断 原文说 Leila 起初 quite down and unhappy、骑车后 depression 缓解，这是受助者的情绪变化。C 项 It is a counseling center. 抓住「情绪低落、好转」的线索，过度推断机构是心理咨询中心，原文从没说它做心理咨询。  借用原文：After a few months of being quite down and unhappy
questions.spoken_text: What do we learn from the passage about rebicycle?

questions.prompt: What do NASA scientists want to learn about?
options: How animals deal with lack of gravity.
How mice interact in a new environment.
How low gravity affects the human body.
How mice imitate human behavior in space.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do NASA scientists want to learn about? 

 【翻译】 NASA的科学家想要了解什么？ 
 A)  动物如何应对失重状态。 
 B)  小鼠如何在新环境中互动。 
 C)  低重力如何影响人体。 
 D)  小鼠如何在太空中模仿人类行为。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） How animals deal with lack of gravity. 
 【定位】 P1 To that end, they have been studying how other species deal with low gravity, specifically focusing on mice. 
 为此，他们一直在研究其他物种如何应对低重力，尤其聚焦于老鼠。 

 【信号】 目的信号 To that end 引出研究指向 。To that end（为此）是承接上文'想了解更多'的目的信号，其后 studying how other species deal with low gravity 正是科学家想了解的内容，是承载答案的那一句。 

 【替换】 how other species deal with low gravity ↔ How animals deal with lack of gravity. other species=animals、low gravity=lack of gravity 的同义替换 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 How mice interact in a new environment. 借用了原文反复出现的 mice 来诱选，但研究内容是'应对低重力'，不是 interact（互相往来）；mice 是真的，interact 是无中生有。  借用原文：specifically focusing on mice 

 C) 原词陷阱 How low gravity affects the human body. 盗用了开头的 the effects of low gravity on the human body 原词，但原文说人体方面'we know quite a bit'（已知不少），科学家'want to learn more'转去研究老鼠，故对人体的研究是旧信息，不是本题问的'想了解什么'。  借用原文：we know quite a bit about the effects of low gravity on the human body 

 D) 未提及 How mice imitate human behavior in space. 拼接了 mice 和太空场景的原词，但原文从未说老鼠 imitate human behavior（模仿人类行为），是凭空捏造的研究内容。
questions.spoken_text: What do NASA scientists want to learn about?

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about the mice at the beginning of the experiment?
options: They found the space in the cage too small to stay in.
They found it difficult to figure out where they were.
They were not used to the low-gravity environment.
They were not sensitive to the changed environment.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say about the mice at the beginning of the experiment? 

 【翻译】 关于实验开始时的小鼠，文章说了什么？ 
 A)  它们发现笼子里的空间太小而无法待在里面。 
 B)  它们发现很难弄清楚自己在哪里。 
 C)  它们不适应低重力环境。 
 D)  它们对改变的环境不敏感。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They were not used to the low-gravity environment. 
 【定位】 P1 As you'll notice in the video, the mice definitely seem uncomfortable at the beginning of the experiment. They move around clumsily, drifting within the small confines of the cage, and do their best to figure out which way is up, but without success. 
 正如你在视频里会看到的，实验开始时老鼠明显显得不适应。它们笨拙地四处移动，在笼子狭小的空间里飘来飘去，竭力想搞清哪边是上，却没成功。 

 【信号】 时间锚 at the beginning + 状态词 uncomfortable 。at the beginning of the experiment 与题干时间锚对应，紧跟的 the mice definitely seem uncomfortable 点明开头状态是'不适应'，后句 do their best to figure out which way is up, but without success 进一步具体化，是答案句。 

 【替换】 the mice definitely seem uncomfortable ↔ They were not used to the low-gravity environment. uncomfortable=not used to 的同义替换 
 do their best to figure out which way is up, but without success ↔ not used to the low-gravity environment 辨不清上下=不适应失重的因果归纳 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 They found the space in the cage too small to stay in. 借了原文 within the small confines of the cage 里的 small 和 cage 原词，但 small confines 只是描述笼子空间小这个客观背景，原文从没说老鼠因此'待不下去（too small to stay in）'，是把背景词偷换成因果结论。  借用原文：drifting within the small confines of the cage 

 B) 偷换概念 They found it difficult to figure out where they were. 盗用原文 figure out which way is up 的 figure out，但原文说的是'辨不清哪边是上（方向/上下）'，不是'搞不清自己身在何处（where they were，位置）'，把'辨方向'偷换成了'辨位置'。  借用原文：do their best to figure out which way is up 

 D) 与原文相反 They were not sensitive to the changed environment. 说老鼠对环境变化不敏感，可原文明说它们 seem uncomfortable、笨拙地辨不清方向，恰恰是对变化高度有反应、很不适应，选项把极性说反了。  借用原文：the mice definitely seem uncomfortable

questions.explanation:
【题目】 What was observed about the mice on the eleventh day of the experiment? 

 【翻译】 实验第十一天观察到小鼠有什么表现？ 
 A)  它们继续像开始时那样行动。 
 B)  它们已经在新环境中感到自在了。 
 C)  它们找到了更多可以参与的活动。 
 D)  它们尝试了一切可能的方法逃离笼子。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） They already felt at home in the new environment. 
 【定位】 P1 The eleventh day of the experiment shows the mice are not just dealing with the gravity change but actually seem to be enjoying it. Several of the mice are observed running around the cage walls. 
 实验第十一天显示，老鼠不只是在应对重力变化，实际上似乎还乐在其中。有几只老鼠被观察到绕着笼壁奔跑。 

 【信号】 时间锚 The eleventh day + 递进 not just…but actually 。The eleventh day of the experiment 与题干时间锚对齐，递进结构 not just dealing with the gravity change but actually seem to be enjoying it 把状态推到'乐在其中'，正是那天观察到的核心情形，是答案句。 

 【替换】 actually seem to be enjoying it ↔ They already felt at home in the new environment. enjoying it=felt at home 的同义替换 
 not just dealing with the gravity change ↔ already felt at home 递进'不止应对'=已超越适应、到自在 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 They continued to behave as they did in the beginning. 说还跟开头一样，但原文第十一天明说它们从 uncomfortable 变到 enjoying it，状态已大变，A 与原文的变化方向相反。它还会蹭第25题'保持作息'的印象诱你混选。  借用原文：the mice definitely seem uncomfortable at the beginning 

 C) 过度推断 They had found a lot more activities to engage in. 借原文 running around the cage walls 让人觉得'活动变多'，但原文只说有几只绕笼壁跑，从没说它们'找到了更多种活动（a lot more activities）'，是把一个动作夸大成'活动种类增多'的过度推断。  借用原文：running around the cage walls 

 D) 未提及 They tried everything possible to escape from the cage. 盗用原文反复出现的 cage，且第23题选项里也埋过'逃笼'的诱饵，但原文从头到尾没说老鼠想 escape（逃跑），它们是适应并享受，不是想逃。

questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did the scientists find about the mice from the experiment? 

 【翻译】 科学家从实验中发现了小鼠的什么情况？ 
 A)  它们在太空中改变了自己的日常习惯。 
 B)  它们一段时间后开始吃得更少。 
 C)  它们的行为表现得就像在地球上一样。 
 D)  它们每天重复自己的活动。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They behaved as if they were on Earth. 
 【定位】 P1 The scientists wanted to see whether the mice would continue doing the same kinds of activities they were observed doing on Earth. The study showed that the mice kept much of their routines intact, including cleaning themselves and eating when hungry. 
 科学家想看看老鼠是否会继续做它们在地球上被观察到的那类活动。研究显示，老鼠的大部分日常作息保持不变，包括给自己清洁和饿了就吃。 

 【信号】 结论信号 The study showed 引出末句发现 。The study showed 是篇章结尾引出结论的信号，其后 the mice kept much of their routines intact 正是实验的总结性发现，是答案句；前句的 on Earth 提供了对照参照。 

 【替换】 the mice kept much of their routines intact ↔ They behaved as if they were on Earth. 保持地球上的作息=表现得像在地球 
 cleaning themselves and eating when hungry ↔ behaved as if they were on Earth 举例的地球式日常→概括为像在地球 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 They changed their routines in space. 盗用原文 routines 和太空场景，但原文明说 kept much of their routines intact（保持作息不变），A 说 changed（改变了），极性相反。  借用原文：the mice kept much of their routines intact 

 B) 原词陷阱 They began to eat less after some time. 盗用原文 eating when hungry 的 eat 原词，但原文只说'饿了就吃'（作息照旧的例子之一），从没说'吃得变少（eat less）'，是把'照常吃'偷换成'吃得少'。  借用原文：eating when hungry 

 D) 偷换概念 They repeated their activities every day. 借'保持日常活动'的意思，但加了 every day（每天）这一原文没有的绝对化限定，原文只说 kept much of their routines（保持大部分作息），并未说'每天重复'，属把范围/频率说死。  借用原文：the mice kept much of their routines intact
